title: The Dorsey band's first flight, to Toronto in 1939
summary: The Dorsey band became the first to fly as a group, on a chartered plane to the Canadian Exposition.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I would like to inject a remembrance that occurs to me that I forgot to mention when we were on the Tommy Dorsey subject. When I was with that band at the Pennsylvania Roof, we were the first band to fly to anybody's knowledge -- we were the first band to fly in an airplane as a group. And they flew us to Toronto, Canada, where from Newark Airport, for the Canadian Exposition -- I think that was the first year of the Canadian Exposition, 1939, in the Fall.

Continuing with the Tommy Dorsey orchestra, flying to the Canadian Exposition -- when we arrived in Newark to leave, we were all a little bit nervous, nobody ever flew before, and of course it was a chartered plane, with a Rolls Royce engine and twin props. Flying today is so common with everybody, I don't think you can appreciate what this was like.

It took us about two and a half to three hours to fly to Toronto from Newark, which is usually about a 40 minute trip today. And going over the mountains, they flew at pretty low altitudes then, into Buffalo and into Toronto, the air currents are pretty bad.
